The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with:
- Large areas of yellowing/chlorosis over most of the leaf
- Brown necrotic patches concentrated on one side and margin
- Pattern appears wedge/V-shaped widest at leaf margin
- No distinct spots, no powdery coating, no fuzzy mycelium

This strongly suggests **Verticillium Wilt** (V-shaped lesion, brown necrosis surrounded by irregular yellowing). Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference Verticillium Wilt image shows asymmetric yellowing and wilting of leaflets, consistent with vascular disease. However, the test image shows more pronounced brown necrosis with irregular surrounding yellowing on a single leaf — matching the description "V-shaped leaf lesions widest at the leaf margin, brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing."

The brown necrotic area is concentrated at the leaf margin and tapers inward (V-shaped), with the rest of the leaf showing diffuse yellowing. No concentric rings (not Early Blight), no spots (not Septoria/Bacterial Speck), no mycelium (not Gray Mold/Late Blight). This pattern is consistent with **Verticillium Wilt**.
